title: Grateful Dead Live at Dance Hall on 1967-09-03
source: RM > C > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a historic 1967 show with outstanding Viola Lee Blues and Alligator, though the Dancin' In The Street rendition falls flat.
ai_review.review: The recording preserves an iconic late‑summer ’67 performance that helped shape the Dead’s early Dark Star ideas. While most of the set is praised – especially the blistering Viola Lee Blues and Alligator – the band’s take on Dancin’ In The Street draws criticism for its rhythm, yet it remains a fascinating historical moment.

ai_rating.rationale: Multiple detailed reviews rate the show 4‑5 stars and highlight several standout performances; recording quality is assumed solid soundboard with no reported issues, yielding a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers do not comment on audio problems; the tape appears to be a typical sound‑board capture with expected clarity and balance.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set runs from average to very good, with Viola Lee Blues and Alligator providing high‑water marks; the early Dark Star ideas emerge during a jam section of Dancin', giving the show historic weight despite its uneven execution.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for great playing on Viola Lee Blues and Alligator; noted as trying hard to rescue Dancin'.
band_member_comments.Bob: Criticized for being rhythmically clueless on Dancin' In The Street.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ work highlighted as outstanding on Viola Lee Blues and Alligator.
